FN-3PS6MZV-1
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 72
Committee: Public Safety and Homeland Sponsor: Representative Patrick Sellers
Security
Analyst: Tiffany Weaver Date: 01/20/2026
House Bill 72 as introduced could increase the administrative obligation of the Department of
Human Resources (DHR) to provide service to children who smell of marijuana as reported by
mandatory reporters.
This bill will also increase the obligations of the Alabama Department of Public Health to: (1)
develop an in-person education course about the dangers of drug and marijuana use around
children to be attended by those who violate the crimes in this bill; and (2) develop education
materials on the dangers of exposing children to marijuana smoke and made available to the
public at no cost.
Further this bill could also increase receipts to the State General Fund and municipal general
funds from fines; increase receipts to the State General Fund, county general funds, municipal
general funds, and other funds to which court costs are deposited; and could increase the
obligations of the State General Fund, district attorneys, and local jails by an undetermined
amount dependent upon the number of persons charged with and convicted of the offenses
provided by this bill and the penalties imposed.

FN-3PS6MZV-2
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 72
Committee: Public Safety and Homeland Sponsor: Representative Patrick Sellers
Security
Analyst: Tiffany Weaver Date: 01/21/2026
House Bill 72 as reported by the Committee on Public Safety and Homeland security could
increase the administrative obligations of the Department of Human Resources (DHR) to
provide services to children who smell of marijuana as reported by mandatory reporters.
This bill will also increase the obligations of the Alabama Department of Public Health by a
department estimated $150,000 to: (1) develop an in-person education course about the dangers
of drug and marijuana use around children to be attended by those who violate the crimes in this
bill; and (2) develop education materials, in collaboration with the Alabama Department of
Mental Health and the Alabama State Law Enforcement, on the dangers of exposing children to
marijuana smoke and made available to the public at no cost.
Further this bill could also increase receipts to the State General Fund and municipal general
funds from fines; increase receipts to the State General Fund, county general funds, municipal
general funds, and other funds to which court costs are deposited; and could increase the
obligations of the State General Fund, district attorneys, and local jails by an undetermined
amount dependent upon the number of persons charged with and convicted of the offenses
provided by this bill and the penalties imposed.
